body.intent: The local ship gate switches on only for an identified flake that repeats, and keeps its full log. Owner, 2026-11-12, after the performance report ('Well that's disappointing'), agreed to file the orchestrator's recommendation. Today one CI flake with no named test ('scripts (4/4) / UNKNOWN STEP' on #498 at ~16:24, auto-filed 01M78960; 29 of the last 30 CI runs were green) marked CI unstable and switched rhiza.ship.localGate (make check, serialized by the machine-wide test lock, ~20 min each) on for every run: about 525 run-minutes lost across 4 runs, run 01M787SV alone ~208 min over 4 local-gate visits (16:32-19:41). Wanted: (1) CI counts as unstable only for a flake that names a failing test and has failed more than once in the window (a step-level or UNKNOWN STEP failure is infra, not a flake); (2) the gate stores its full output as a file in the run dir and the journal points to it, instead of keeping only the last ~2 KB (today the failing test's name was cut off, so every gate-fix agent reran the whole suite); (3) the gate's reason names the flake and when it stops applying. Evidence: perf report ~/orchestrator/perf-2026-11-12/report-prospective.md; related bug 01M78CSH (rootguard false positive that made every gate fail).
